title: CI CD And Secrets Security Foundation
goal: Add a first-class assessment slice for CI/CD pipeline exposure, credential hygiene, artifact handling, and secret-management weaknesses so AegisPT can assess more of the real software delivery attack surface.
scope: Implement a bounded CI/CD and secrets-security assessment path that can analyze authorized GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or uploaded pipeline configurations plus linked repository metadata where available. The first slice covers: over-privileged pipeline tokens, secret exposure in pipeline definitions or artifacts, poisoned pipeline execution preconditions, insecure self-hosted runner exposure, artifact and cache leakage, weak branch/protection assumptions visible from pipeline config, and selected repository/pipeline secret-hygiene findings. Reuse the existing repo integration and protected-secret boundaries where possible. Keep pipeline execution, live pipeline mutation, and exploit chaining out of scope.
generation_reason: The audit found that AegisPT already has repository integration and CI-trigger backlog items, but not an actual CI/CD security assessment slice. OWASP's CI/CD Top 10 and WrongSecrets both point to a major attack surface around credential hygiene, pipeline poisoning, and secret handling that is currently missing from the product.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Assessment only. Do not execute pipelines, modify repository settings, rotate credentials, or create CI jobs in this slice.
notes: Secrets must continue to use existing protected handling patterns.
This task assesses pipeline security posture; it does not replace backlog-62 or backlog-63.
Canonical finding schema fields must remain unchanged.

success_criteria: A bounded CI/CD and secrets-security assessment path exists.
Pipeline definitions or linked repo metadata can surface credential-hygiene, artifact-exposure, and poisoned-pipeline precondition findings.
Secret-hygiene findings are evidence-backed and avoid raw secret disclosure.
Tests cover unsupported pipeline types, missing configs, and protected-output behavior.
No live pipeline execution or mutation is introduced.
must_not_touch: pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: CI/CD security assessment stays read-only and evidence-backed.
Secret-hygiene findings do not leak raw secrets.
Unsupported pipeline states are explicit and safe.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
The read-only CI/CD assessment boundary is documented.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with CI/CD and secrets assessment implementation and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with the CI/CD security baseline and remaining limits.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
